releases.name: 0.1.3-alpha - 2026-10-31
releases.body:
### Fixed

- Frame captures (`RPS5E_CAPTURE_FRAMES`) of GTA V replay again instead of hanging the GPU. While a capture recorded, GPU results copied straight into guest memory were later taken for CPU writes and recorded; the replay wrote them over its own GPU results, which differ where GPU work orders its atomics differently, and the mixed ray-tracing tree sent a shader into an endless loop. GPU results now reach guest memory through copies the capture sees while it records.
- Silent Hill 2 (Remake) no longer hangs the GPU after START GAME. A small compute write (a 4-byte counter in reused transient memory) at an address where a render target once kept its fast-clear metadata was taken for a metadata clear, which overwrote the counter and left a GPU loop running for billions of iterations; only writes that cover a whole metadata slice count as clears now (`RPS5E_WHOLE_METADATA_WRITES`).
- Silent Hill 2 (Remake): the ray-tracing acceleration-structure build after START GAME no longer loops forever on the GPU. Compute shaders whose buffer record count comes from a value computed at run time (here an atomic counter read back with `v_readfirstlane`) were skipped, so the sort before th

releases.name: 0.1.2-alpha
releases.body:
### Added

- Games run straight from disk images of game dumps, without extracting them: exFAT images (`.exfat`, also inside an MBR or GPT partition), `.ffpfsc` containers (a PS5 PFS image holding a compressed exFAT image) and UFS2 images (`.ffpkg` dumps made on the console). The game folder is found anywhere inside the image.
- The launcher lists `.exfat` and `.ffpfsc` files with their title, version and icon, and its file pickers accept them; `info-pkg` and `install-pkg` read them too.
- PS5 fake packages ("\x7FFIH" packages made in plain-text mode) run straight from the `.pkg`, without extracting them: the Kraken-compressed game image is decoded on demand, and the package's metadata (title, version, icon, `sce_sys/param.json`) is read from it. `info-pkg` and the launcher show them; PS5 retail packages are still reported as encrypted. Silent Hill 2 (Remake) starts from its 48 GB package and reaches the main menu and the New Game settings at about 1 fps; it can still crash right after the start screen (with `RPS5E_LABELS_AT_EOP=through` it does not), and loading a new game stalls.
- Kraken-compressed PFSC files (the PS5 per-file compression) are read; other PS5 compression format

releases.name: 0.1.1-alpha
releases.body:
### Added

- Display resolution setting (720p, 1080p or 2160p) in the launcher, the "Run with..." dialog, `--display-resolution` and `RPS5E_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION`: games that ask the console for the TV's resolution are told the chosen one, as a PS5 on that TV would answer; the default stays 2160p.
- PlayGo: `scePlayGoRequestOptionalChunk`, `scePlayGoGetRequiredDisc`, `scePlayGoRequestNextChunk`, `scePlayGoSnapshot` and `scePlayGoSetInstallSpeed2` are implemented. The library now tracks its initialized and open-handle state (`NOT_INITIALIZED`, `ALREADY_INITIALIZED`, `BAD_HANDLE` after close), remembers the install speed that was set, and answers a chunk-id count query made without a list buffer.

### Performance

- GTA V in the city: the longest stalls are much shorter (about 2.5 s instead of 10 s) and driving stutters far less. The frame rate in the city is still low (about 7 fps now that the ray-traced reflections are drawn) and far from playable.
- Wave64 compute shaders on 32-wide GPUs (NVIDIA): lane stacks and register spills stay in registers, ballots share one exchange, and programs from 16 VGPRs run split; the ray traversal of GTA V takes about a third of its former GPU time.

# NgpCraft Emulator v3.15 - what's new

This release is mostly about the built-in BIOS, the one the emulator uses when you have no
`bios.bin` (and the one the web player always uses). It now behaves much more like the real
console BIOS. macOS users also get proper app packaging and Finder support.

## Built-in BIOS: much closer to the real one

Many thanks to **Napomex**, who compared our built-in BIOS with the real one game by game and sent
us a detailed report with a fix for each problem. This work started from that report.

We then ran 123 cartridges for one minute each, with button presses, under both the real BIOS and
the built-in one, and compared every frame. About 70% of them now play frame for frame like they
do with the real BIOS, up from about 25%.

- **Fewer crashes.** Puzzle Link, Puzzle Link 2, Magical Drop Pocket and Densha de Go! 2 could
  crash, especially while saving. The built-in BIOS let the game interrupt it in the middle of a
  system call. Found by Napomex.
- **Saving is safer.** When a game erased all of its save memory, the built-in BIOS did not wait
  for the cartridge to finish and could freeze the game. It now waits like the real BIOS. This
  affects Ki

NgpCraft Emulator v3.9.0 - what's new
This release is about playing two players over the internet. It is still being tested, but the
first results are encouraging. If you play online, both of you should update, and please tell us
how it goes.

Online play in mirror mode should be smoother
Less input lag at the start of a match. The player who finished loading first used to start alone and wait for the other one. That wait made the emulator think the connection was slower than it really was, and it could add noticeable delay to that player's controls for several minutes. Both sides now start together. This idea comes from Blueteemo, who proposed it in pull request #26. Thank you!
Fewer freezes on a connection that loses packets. Your button presses are now also sent a second way, repeated several times, so a single lost packet should no longer freeze both screens. In our tests on a deliberately bad connection, most of the short freezes went away.
If the other player has an older version, the match should still work, just without these improvements.

releases.body:
# Zaxnes 0.2.0

Independent project, not affiliated with Geod Studio or Nintendo. NES is a trademark of Nintendo.

## New

- **Import from 3dSen.** If you own 3dSen, `File > Import from 3dSen…` (or `--import-3dsen <folder>`) copies the game profiles from your installation into your Zaxnes profiles folder. Nothing is downloaded and no profile ships with Zaxnes.
- **`profiles` folder next to `Zaxnes.exe`.** Profiles placed there are always loaded, in portable mode or not. A file with the same name in your user profiles folder takes priority.
- **English or French interface.** English by default; switch in `Options > Interface`. The change applies immediately.

## Improved

- Sharper shadows of thin details: status-bar text and other fine strokes are much more readable (4096 shadow map).
- Unlit faces are darker, closer to the expected look.
- Anti-aliasing and the resolution scale now really change the rendering.
- Starting in fullscreen no longer shows a black screen.
- Ctrl+C in the console no longer closes the emulator; the console is used only by `--help`, `--list-profiles` and `--import-3dsen`.

## Removed

- The decorative CRT TV around the picture, and its third-party model.

track losing one transition per revolution, a same-value 6522 store that

of a datasheet differs from another emulator's, the divergence is now
documented in the code rather than silently aligned. Every hardware claim
carries

# POM2 v1.0.0

The first stable release: the Apple ][, ][+, //e, //c and //c Plus, in NTSC
and PAL, with the cards, media and tools listed in the README.

- **Your data stays put:** an unreadable `state.cfg`, a disk on an unplugged
  drive, the printouts of a second window and the browser's saved sessions
  are no longer lost.
- **Accelerators keep real time:** video, Disk II, SoftCard, Liron and
  paddles stay at 1 MHz under a TransWarp, a Zip or the //c Plus.
- **Closer to the hardware:** composite colour, `.nib` sync, SSI263 speech,
  paddle timers and the ][+ cursor.
- **Bundled disks:** A2 File Cmd 1.0, Dirtbike 1.1, ChromaBreak 1.1,
  Micro-Sokoban 1.3 and DIX.
- **macOS:** relative paths and the first launch of a downloaded copy work.

# POM2 v0.9.8

- **Sessions restore the whole machine:** profile, firmware, cards and

releases.body:
## ✨ A calmer, clearer CosmoU

CosmoU 0.13 reworks the whole interface. All the features are still there, just sorted better, so every window and every theme feels like one product: easy to understand on the first start, calm with a big library, readable from the sofa.

## What changed

- **Play is always the strongest button** – in Covers, Grid, the Wii U Look and the game details. Details and the other actions are quieter.
- **Grid** – a calm banner: the cover sharp in front of its own softly blurred colours, instead of a giant pixelated picture.

Install over v0.1.4 (or update in the app): saves, packs and settings are kept. Shaders already on your phone carry over in seconds, no shader update needed.

**New**
- **Pokémon Pokopia (`0400A3A01EE4C000`) is playable**: about 60 fps on the system driver and on Turnip. Game resolution works for it.
- **Text boxes**: when a game asks you to type, a text box opens (OK or Cancel). Before, the game could get stuck.
- **FSR 1 upscaling** (optional): in the game's panel › Upscaling, with a sharpness slider. Sharper picture when the game is scaled up, e.g. at Phone 720p.
- **Donkey Kong Bananza (`040074A01BF12000`): dynamic resolution works**, thanks to correct GPU timing (Game settings › GPU timing).
- **Phone Prepare** builds only the shaders a game needs when the app knows them (8,157 instead of 131,426 for Pokémon Pokopia (`0400A3A01EE4C000`)).

**Known issues**
- Pokémon Pokopia (`0400A3A01EE4C000`): the sky is black.

releases.name: v0.1.4
releases.body:
## Banana Native v0.1.4

Install over v0.1.3: saves, packs and settings are kept. No shader update is needed.

- **In-app updates.** From this version on, the app checks this page when it starts and offers new releases in a popup (Update or Later). It downloads the APK from this page and checks it before Android asks you to install it. Settings › Check for updates checks right away.
- **`0400C3F00006E000`: Prepare no longer stops at "rewriting the game code" (#20).** That step now needs about a fifth of the memory (0.5 GB instead of about 3 GB), so it finishes on phones with other apps open. If Prepare stopped for you, tap Retry.
- **No more false "Pack from other tools" chip** on packs this app made. Packs made by earlier versions count as current; nothing has to be prepared again.

Needs Android 13+, a Snapdragon (Adreno) phone with 12 GB of RAM or more, and your own dump. Experimental: back up your saves. Download only from this page. No games, keys or shaders are included. GPL-3.0-or-later.

## Banana Native v0.1.3

Install over v0.1.2: saves, packs and settings are kept.

- **`040074A01BF12000`: 30 fps on Turnip at Phone 1080p (was about 20; #5, #16).** The upscaler shader is rewritten for Adreno and the GPU clock no longer drops on Turnip. Phone 1080p is the default again; if you set Phone 720p for v0.1.2, switch back in Game settings › Game resolution. 60 fps is a later step.
- **One shader update after installing.** The app does it by itself when opened (112 shaders for `040074A01BF12000`, 175 for `0400C3F00006E000`); the game can start once its card says **Ready**. The update pauses while the phone is too hot and goes on once it cools.
- The build tag no longer shows the build time.

Needs Android 13+, a Snapdragon (Adreno) phone with 12 GB of RAM or more, and your own dump. Experimental: back up your saves. Download only from this page. No games, keys or shaders are included. GPL-3.0-or-later.

## Banana Native v0.1.2 (hotfix)

Install over v0.1.1: saves, packs and settings are kept.

### Fixes
- **Prepare shaders on shared storage:** Prepare no longer stops with "Operation not permitted" after splitting the game's files (it now writes the `split` folder in place instead of renaming it). If Prepare failed there on v0.1.1, run it again.
- **GPU driver install no longer crashes the app:** pick the driver .zip, it installs in the background, and any problem is shown as a message. The app no longer scans the Download folder on its own.
- **Add game takes dumps in any layout:** base only, update only, or base + update, as a folder or a `.nup`. Each game shows as one card (old duplicate cards are merged), with its build shown on Home.
- **Same game code under another version number:** a dump whose code is identical to a supported version (same build IDs) plays with that version's pack, for example `0400C3F00006E000` 1.8.1. A different build gets a clear message naming its version and the supported one.
- **Picking a file on Xiaomi / HyperOS phones:** a `.nup` picked with HyperOS's file picker no longer fails with a doubled path (`/storage/emulated/0/storage/emulated/0/…`).

## Banana Native v0.1.1

### New
- **NUP files:** add a game straight from one `.nup` file (base, update and DLC in one file), no unpacking. Add game › A .nup file.
- **Emulator frontends:** ES-DE, Daijisho, Pegasus and others can start a game directly. Setup: [frontend guide](https://github.com/moceure/BananaNative/blob/v0.1.1/android/FRONTENDS.md).
- **Incremental shader updates:** from now on, when shaders change, only the changed ones are rebuilt in the background, and Play stays available. A pack made before versioned updates shows "Shaders need one update": run Prepare shaders once, then updates stay small.
- **`0400C3F00006E000` can be prepared on the phone** (about 16-30 minutes; not yet tested on many phones, reports welcome).
- **`0400C3F00006E000` uses about 1 GiB less RAM**, and no longer crashes during loads in docked mode.
- **Fewer stutters, less memory:** large GPU memory pools are mapped in parts, only where the GPU uses them, and large files in a `.nup` are unpacked to storage instead of into RAM.

# Changes

* Fix build issues with zlib v1.3.1
* Fix audio not working when using the AppImage (thank you @Samueru-sama)
* Fix screenshots causing a crash on Linux

* Update mupen64plus-core and LZMA SDK

The netplay servers hosted by @loganmc10 have been changed into something incompatible with RMG, due to these changes RMG will no longer have any hosted servers, but self-hosting isn't too difficult as I've outlined in the new netplay section in the README.

# Changes
* Fix AppImage icon not working since v0.7.1 (thank you @Samueru-sama)
* Fix desktop file causing a crash on Budgie (thank you @jpleatherland)
* Fix memory pak from player 2, 3 and 4 not saving correctly (see https://github.com/mupen64plus/mupen64plus-core/commit/3c2955c910d535b3da7721c66b5b8e01b3361160)

* Add plugin settings shortcuts to the toolbar
* Update mupen64plus-video-GLideN64, SDL_net and SDL_GameControllerDB

# Changes
* Fix exit confirmation dialog showing when launching RMG with '--nogui'
* Fix emulation not shutting down properly on exit in some cases
* Fix remaining issues with the 'Auto-Configure' button state in the configuration dialog of RMG-Input
* Fix asserts being enabled when building the RelWithDebInfo configuration
* Fix uninitialized variable being read in the configuration dialog of GLideN64
* Add checkbox to drag and drop confirmation dialog to prevent future confirmations
* Move 'Ask for confirmation on exit' setting to the emulation tab in the settings dialog
* Improve 'Input Device' UI element in the configuration GUI of RMG-Input by allowing it to take more width
* Improve refresh and join button state in the Netplay Session Browser dialog

# Changes
* Fix drag and drop not working in the flatpak
* Fix hotkeys dialog in RMG-Input not showing native face button names
* Fix cheat dialog in RMG not allowing users to set cheat option since v0.7.2

* Fix top row of UI elements in the configuration GUI of RMG-Input not being aligned properly
* Add tooltips to the top row of UI elements in the configuration GUI of RMG-Input
* Add 'Game Type' to the 'ROM Information' dialog

releases.name: Ryujinx-Nextendo 1.10.2
releases.body:
## Mario Kart 8 Deluxe online fixed (2306-0502)
- 1.10.0 started deferring every Bsd poll with a finite timeout. That broke the NEX connection of Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, which failed with error 2306-0502. MK8's ordinary NEX polls now use the blocking path again, as in 1.9.9; eventfd polls and the finite-timeout optimization of other games (Portal 2 and others) are unchanged (#75)

## New online games
- SpeedRunners 2: Nextendo routes scoped to the game, and a TLS peer reset during the handshake is now returned to the game as an SSL error instead of stopping the emulator (#79)
- Just Dance 2022: Nextendo routes, exact-build TLS trust patch with native certificate verification kept on, and blocking UDP receives no longer hold the shared socket thread (#74)
- Ultimate Chicken Horse 1.13.13.765: online support (#68)
- Guilty Gear Strive: online services redirected to Nextendo (#77)
- Nintendo Switch Online Classics: versions set for NES, SNES, Game Boy, Game Boy Advance, Nintendo 64 and SEGA Genesis, plus a Windows JIT fix (#69)

## Other fixes
- Steam Deck: touchscreen, rumble and gyro input (#76)
- NPLN online patches are loaded from the signed patch catalog (#73)
- nim: the IShopServic

releases.body:
# PS5PCEM 0.3.4

**This release fixes a launcher regression that prevented games from starting
in packaged installations. Updating both the launcher and runner is recommended.**
It also adds working font rendering, fixes Jurassic Park's font-atlas startup,
implements MemoryPool and AMPR counters, and expands RDNA2 shader support.

These are the changes since **0.3.3**, covering the October 7–9 development
commits. The portable ZIP and per-user installer include the updated launcher,
runner and PKG extractor. All three applications and the installer carry
timestamped SHA-256 Authenticode signatures using the same
**Artur Strazewicz / PS5PCEM** certificate as the previous release.

## Important launcher fix

The launcher could pass its own executable path as the runner's working
directory because a shortened Windows path lacked its terminating zero.
Windows rejected `CreateProcessW` with `ERROR_DIRECTORY` before the game
started. The development `zig-out\bin` layout masked the defect, while ordinary
portable and installed layouts exposed it. The directory is now correctly
terminated.

If Windows refuses to create the runner process, the launcher now displays
Windows' explanation, the

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.8.6a — Windows hotfix

**Windows only.** This release contains a single asset for Windows x64. Everything else is
v0.9.8.6 unchanged.

---

## Why the v0.9.8.6 Windows package refused to start on AMD graphics cards

On Windows, AMD's Vulkan driver reports **128 bytes** of push constants — the amount Vulkan itself
guarantees. Every driver this renderer had been developed against reports 256.

The 3D scene shader packed 208 bytes into that block: the projection matrix, the light parameters
and the fog colour, re-sent on every single draw call. The renderer's device selection therefore
required 256 bytes, found 128, rejected the GPU, and the program exited — the start-up artwork
flashed and disappeared, no settings window, no game, no message. Nothing in the picture was wrong;
the renderer simply refused to open the device.

The report that surfaced this was a Steam Deck running Windows 11, whose AMD APU driver reports 128
as well — but the same limit applies to Radeon cards and Ryzen APUs on Windows generally, not to one
machine.

parameters and t

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.8.6x — Linux and macOS

**This release replaces both `v0.9.8.6l` (Linux) and `v0.9.8.6m` (macOS).** It contains three
assets: Linux, macOS for Apple Silicon, and macOS for Intel Macs. There is no Windows package: the
Windows build is unchanged since v0.9.8.6 and does not need this update.

---

## Fixed in both packages

**The in-game settings panel ignored the mouse and the keyboard on Linux and macOS.**

Press Tab and the panel opened, but nothing in it responded: no hover highlight, no clicks, no arrow
keys, no Enter. The panel's input feed was Windows-only — the whole block that reads the pointer
position, the mouse buttons and the key states sat behind `#ifdef _WIN32`, with no equivalent for the
other platforms, so on Linux and macOS only the mouse wheel was ever delivered. It now reads the
platform's per-frame input snapshot, which both backends already maintain: pointer position, three
mouse buttons, Ctrl/Shift/Alt and a full key table (arrows, Tab, Enter, Escape, Home/End, Page Up/Down,
Insert/Delete, Backspace, Space, A/C/V/X/Z, digits and the keypad).

Verified by hand on both platforms: the panel responds to the mouse, to keyboard navigation, and to

This is v0.9.8.6 with the Linux fixes only. Everything else is unchanged.

---

## Why the v0.9.8.6 Linux package refused to start

The v0.9.8.6 Linux build could not run on Steam Deck, Ubuntu 24.04, or most other current
distributions. It exited instantly — no window, no log, nothing to report.

The cause was the build environment, not the emulator and not your hardware. Linux packages are
compiled by GitHub Actions, and the runner we asked for is `ubuntu-latest`: a label GitHub keeps
pointed at the newest Ubuntu release. That image moved forward under us, so the package came out
linked against glibc 2.43 while SteamOS and the current Ubuntu LTS are older. The dynamic loader
rejects such a binary before the first line of our code runs, which is why the failure looked like a

# Model 3-Vulkan Release Notes

## v0.9.8.6m — macOS only (2026-10-30)

> **This release is for macOS only.** It contains one asset, `Model3-Vulkan.v0.9.8.6m.for.macOS.tar.gz`.
> There is no Windows or Linux build in this release, and none is needed: nothing outside the
> macOS platform layer changed since v0.9.8.6. The `m` suffix marks the macOS build of 0.9.8.6;
> the Windows and Linux builds keep the 0.9.8.6 number.

**Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.8.6m makes the macOS build start again.** v0.9.8.6 refused to launch with
"Vulkan 1.3 required" (`VkResult -7`) on every Mac that has been tried; this release fixes the
three macOS-only defects behind that message.

### Fixed (macOS)

* **Startup no longer fails with `VkResult -7`.** The preflight asked for `VK_KHR_portability_enumeration`, an extension the Vulkan *loader* synthesises. The macOS package loads MoltenVK directly through volk with no loader in between, so the request was rejected before any device was looked at. The extension is now requested only when the implementation actually lists it, and the portability flag is set together with it.

emulators.latest_body:
## AMD and Vulkan fixes

This update focuses on AMD shader correctness and Vulkan synchronization. These are targeted fixes, not a guarantee that every AMD game or rendering issue is resolved.

- [#273](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/273) keeps depth-compare images floating-point and makes failed atomic compare-exchange operations feed their returned value into the next retry. On AMD's proprietary Vulkan driver, fragment shuffles use a broadcast fallback. Driver optimization is disabled only for compute shaders `EFF3CCBE1438679D` and `F9EA14A22394F5B1`, which have reported multi-minute compilation stalls.
- [#295](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/295) splits misaligned 64-bit and 128-bit storage-buffer accesses into 32-bit words instead of reading or writing the wrong vector. Vulkan barriers now cover indirect dispatch arguments, make compute writes visible to subsequent graphics work, and replace stale wait-for-idle event reuse with a memory barrier.

These changes have compiler, regression-test, and validation evidence. The combined fixes have not been verified in affected AMD gameplay. Shuffle fallbacks and unoptimized shaders can cost runtime performance; stro

### Performance and synchronization
- Integrated the reviewed Frizti performance ports: cached storage-buffer bindings, direct native uniform-bank uploads, and batched command-page readbacks.
- Reduced unnecessary writer tracking and submitted native desktop GPU work earlier, while preserving conservative synchronization for macro reads and semaphore waits.
- Added explicit GPU-to-host visibility before buffer readback.

releases.name: Lichii nx2 build 75 (c9ebb5c)
releases.body:
## What's new since build 70

### Game fixes
- **The green-hat kid adventure:** it now boots, gets through the intro and plays. It used to abort about 20 s after launch, on a 64-bit wait-on-address the kernel rejected (upstream Eglantine #567 is ported). About 80 shaders it couldn't run before now translate, so the white screen is gone and the world renders (#87).
- **Star Fox:** gameplay runs at 60 fps instead of 30. Ampere GPU timestamps are now reported in nanoseconds (#84).

### Updater
- The in-app updater now checks Lichii's GitHub releases and picks the right download for your platform (#82).

### Diagnostics (all off by default)
- The frame dump can also record every texture a pass or compute dispatch samples (`EDEN_NX2_FRAME_DUMP_SAMPLED=1`), and `EDEN_NX2_REJECT_HASH` switches off specific shaders for A/B tests (#87).

### Known issues
- **Green-hat kid:** outdoor areas have far too much fog and glow, much hazier than on console. We're working on it.
- **Green-hat kid:** performance is low, about 12–22 fps on a Ryzen 5900X with an RTX 3080, and three rare shaders are still unsupported.
- **Star Fox on RTX 50-series GPUs** can still lose the GPU device after a scene change

releases.name: Lichii nx2 build 70 (286117c)
releases.body:
## What's new since build 65

### Game fixes
- **Star Fox:** it now renders instead of showing a black screen. Its DLSS network goes through Lichii's de-jitter stand-in, which stops the heavy smearing and stretched geometry (#45, #46). The `ULDC.U16` shader lowering is in (#45). Controller input works through HID command 300 (#64). The MSVC build of its colour match is fixed (#76).
- **Donkey Kong Bananza:** fixes the crash after cutscenes and cuts the stutter from command-page draining on the split GPU thread (#70). Atomic compute shaders, pacing and descriptor fixes are in (#45). It runs well, though not at a locked 60 fps yet.
- **Kirby Air Riders:** fixes the white world (#56). Texture arrays with separate samplers no longer break, and the pipeline cache is now v50, so shaders rebuild once (#65). Shader translation is faster, and pipelines the game is waiting on now build immediately instead of queueing, so race stalls are shorter (#71).
- **Mario Tennis Fever:** fixes the device loss when the first court loads (#38).
